title: Commitment leak guard and proportional warmup smoothing for Dedicated fleet
author: Ava Trivedi
release_notes: Introduces a commitment-leak detection/auditor and a proportional warmup smoothing policy for Dedicated fleet autoscaling. Improves stability during rapid decommissions and initial warmup by smoothing reserved capacity application. No public API changes.
description:
Background and motivation:
We observed two recurring issues on Dedicated fleets: 1) short-lived reservation/commitment leaks when nodes are decommissioned quickly (causes temporary over-commit reporting and unexpected token/burst behavior), and 2) oscillatory warmup effects where newly provisioned capacity applies immediately and then gets trimmed back during subsequent reconciliations, causing latency blips and missed throughput guarantees.

This PR implements a two-part mitigation: a Commitment Leak Guard (an auditor process that detects and reconciles orphaned/residual commitment state across the reservation ledger) and a Proportional Warmup Smoothing policy (applies reserved capacity in a weighted ramp over a configurable warmup window and biases the autoscaler to respect recent utilization history to avoid oscillation).

Design summary:
- commitment_guard.go: background reconciler that periodically scans active reservations, cross-validates with node leases, and emits corrective actions (soft-decrement vs forced-reclaim) with safety cooldowns to avoid double-reclaims. Includes exponential backoff and a configurable toleration window to account for transient network partitions.
- warmup_window.go: implements a proportional ramp function that computes an "applied_commit_fraction" based on age since reservation + recent utilization EWMA. The function is pluggable as an autoscaler policy and exposes knobs: warmup_seconds, smoothing_alpha, min_fraction.
- telemetry hooks: emits "commitment_leak_detected", "commitment_reclaimed", "warmup_fraction_applied" metrics with tenant and pool dimensions; updated usage_reporter to include sample of applied fraction per reconciliation.
- simulation harness: extended sim_runner to run scenarios with rapid decommissions and spike-on-warmup to validate SLO stability.

Checklist:
- [x] Unit tests for leak detection heuristics and reclaim path
- [x] Integration e2e sim for warmup smoothing vs baseline autoscaler
- [x] Telemetry dashboard snippets and alert rules added to docs
- [x] Backwards compatible: default policy disabled for fleets with legacy autoscaler opt-out

Testing and results:
- Local e2e simulation: sustained 99th p50 latency improvement during aggressive capacity churn (reduction in latency spikes by ~38% in sim), reduced transient over-commit alerts by 86% in simulated failure windows.
- CI: initial lint/test run hit a race in warmup window update; fixed by adding a small sync point in reconciliation loop. All tests now pass.

Related items:
- Linear ENG-4821: Dedicated stability workstream
- Related PRs: small telemetry formatting change (not included here) and a docs-only follow-up to show policy configuration examples.

Merging notes:
- Feature guarded behind fleet feature flag: "dedicated.commitment_guard_enabled" and autoscaler policy selector (defaults to off for existing production fleets). Ops may flip the flag incrementally during rollout.
